isoDesc: The organization shall determine external and internal issues that are relevant to its purpose and that affect its ability to achieve the intended outcome(s) of its information security management system.
name: Understanding the organization and its context
notes: Conduct a formal SWOT or PESTLE analysis annually. Document internal issues (culture, resources, processes) and external issues (legal, regulatory, tech market). Review the context formally during the annual Management Review.

isoDesc: The organization shall determine interested parties that are relevant to the ISMS, the requirements of these interested parties, and which of these requirements will be addressed.
name: Understanding needs and expectations of interested parties
notes: Maintain an 'Interested Parties Register' logging internal stakeholders (staff, board) and external stakeholders (regulators, customers, vendors). Detail their specific security, privacy, and compliance requirements (e.g., SLA uptime needs, GDPR compliance).

isoDesc: The organization shall determine the boundaries and applicability of the ISMS to establish its scope.
name: Determining the scope of the information security management system
notes: Document the formal ISMS Scope Statement. Explicitly define what physical locations, business units, services, and networks are included and excluded. Ensure the scope directly addresses the context (4.1) and interested party requirements (4.2).

isoDesc: The organization shall establish, implement, maintain and continually improve an information security management system, including the processes needed and their interactions.
name: Information security management system
notes: This wraps the entire standard. Ensure processes (risk management, internal audit, incident response) interact harmoniously. Map the core processes in a high-level flowchart or operating model diagram within the ISMS Manual.

isoDesc: Top management shall demonstrate leadership and commitment with respect to the ISMS by directing and supporting persons to contribute to the effectiveness of the ISMS and promoting continual improvement.
name: Leadership and commitment
notes: Ensure senior leadership (C-Suite/Board) actively signs off on the Information Security Policy. Evidence leadership commitment through meeting minutes, budget allocations for security tools, and explicit alignment of security objectives with business strategy.

isoDesc: Top management shall establish an information security policy that is appropriate to the purpose of the organization and provides a framework for setting information security objectives.
name: Policy
notes: Publish a high-level 'Information Security Policy'. It must explicitly state commitment to fulfilling requirements and continual improvement. It does not need to be deeply technical—keep it accessible to all staff and publicly accessible if needed.

isoDesc: Top management shall ensure that the responsibilities and authorities for roles relevant to information security are assigned and communicated.
name: Organizational roles, responsibilities and authorities
notes: Document a formal RACI chart or Organizational Chart defining who owns the ISMS. Define role descriptions for the CISO/Security Manager, Risk Owners, Asset Owners, and the steering committee. Communicate these designations clearly.

isoDesc: When planning for the ISMS, the organization shall consider issues, requirements, and determine the risks and opportunities that need to be addressed.
name: General (Actions to address risks and opportunities)
notes: Ensure the risk assessment explicitly covers not just negative threats (risks) but positive security opportunities (e.g., migrating to a secure cloud platform to reduce physical security overhead). Tie these directly back to the context defined in 4.1.

isoDesc: The organization shall define and apply an information security risk assessment process that establishes and maintains information security risk criteria.
name: Information security risk assessment
notes: Publish a 'Risk Assessment Methodology' document. Define explicit criteria for calculating Impact and Likelihood (e.g., 5x5 matrix). Define the explicit risk acceptance threshold (e.g., 'Medium risks require mitigation plan, Low risks are accepted').

isoDesc: The organization shall define and apply an information security risk treatment process to select appropriate information security risk treatment options.
name: Information security risk treatment
notes: For every assessed risk exceeding the threshold, map it to a treatment option (Mitigate, Transfer/Insure, Avoid, Accept). Produce a formal Risk Treatment Plan (RTP). Crucially, map the chosen mitigations directly to the 93 operational controls in Annex A.

isoDesc: The organization shall produce a Statement of Applicability (SoA) that contains the necessary controls and justification for inclusions or exclusions.
name: Statement of Applicability (SoA)
notes: Draft the formal SoA spreadsheet or document. It must list all 93 controls from ISO 27001 Annex A, explicitly state 'Applicable' or 'Not Applicable', provide brief justification for either status, and map to the specific risk treatment it resolves.

isoDesc: The organization shall establish information security objectives at relevant functions and levels. The objectives shall be measurable (if practicable).
name: Information security objectives and planning to achieve them
notes: Define specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART) security objectives for the year (e.g., 'Achieve >95% completion rate of security training', 'Maintain zero critical data breaches'). Document action plans to achieve them.

isoDesc: The organization shall determine and provide the resources needed for the establishment, implementation, maintenance and continual improvement of the ISMS.
name: Resources
notes: Evidence that management has provided sufficient resources. This includes financial budget for security tools, headcount for security staffing, and dedicated time for personnel to perform risk assessments and audits.

isoDesc: The organization shall determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its information security performance.
name: Competence
notes: Maintain job descriptions detailing required security qualifications for sensitive roles (e.g., CISO requires CISSP or equivalent). Maintain records of training, certifications, and education verifying staff competence.

isoDesc: Persons doing work under the organization's control shall be aware of the information security policy and their contribution to the effectiveness of the ISMS.
name: Awareness
notes: Implement mandatory annual security awareness training for all staff and contractors. Content must explicitly mention the Information Security Policy, the implications of non-compliance, and how to report incidents. Track completion metrics.

isoDesc: The organization shall determine the need for internal and external communications relevant to the information security management system.
name: Communication
notes: Draft a 'Communications Plan' that outlines: on what topics to communicate (incidents, policy updates), when to communicate, with whom (regulators, clients, staff), and who is explicitly authorized to communicate (PR, Legal, C-Suite).

isoDesc: The organization's ISMS shall include documented information required by this document and determined as necessary for the effectiveness of the ISMS.
name: Documented information
notes: Establish document control rules. Ensure every ISMS policy, procedure, and manual has a version number, author, approver, and date. Ensure confidential ISMS documents are protected from unauthorized viewing or tampering.

isoDesc: The organization shall plan, implement and control the processes needed to meet information security requirements, and to implement the actions determined in Clause 6.
name: Operational planning and control
notes: This links the planning (Clause 6) to the actual doing. Ensure the Risk Treatment Plans are actively executed. Control planned changes, and review the consequences of unintended changes, taking action to mitigate adverse effects.

isoDesc: The organization shall perform information security risk assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur.
name: Information security risk assessment (Operational)
notes: Do not let the risk register stagnate. Formally schedule risk assessment reviews at least annually, and immediately following major architectural changes, cloud migrations, or significant security incidents. Retain documented evidence of the results.

isoDesc: The organization shall implement the information security risk treatment plan. The organization shall retain documented information of the results.
name: Information security risk treatment (Operational)
notes: Evidence the active implementation of the RTP. If a treatment was 'Deploy EDR tools by Q3', provide the project closure sign-offs or active deployed tooling proof. Retain records showing the progression and completion of risk treatments.

isoDesc: The organization shall evaluate the information security performance and the effectiveness of the ISMS. It shall determine what needs to be monitored and measured.
name: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
notes: Define explicit KPIs/metrics for ISMS performance (e.g., 'Phishing click rate < 5%', 'Critical patches deployed < 7 days'). Collect the data routinely and present the analysis to management to prove whether security controls are actually working.

isoDesc: The organization shall conduct internal audits at planned intervals to provide information on whether the ISMS conforms to requirements and is effectively implemented.
name: Internal audit
notes: Establish a 3-year audit programme covering all clauses and controls. Use independent auditors (internal staff outside the ISMS chain of command, or external consultants). Document the audit findings and formally assign nonconformities.

isoDesc: Top management shall review the organization's information security management system at planned intervals to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.
name: Management review
notes: Conduct the 'Management Review Meeting' at least annually. Follow the strict agenda defined by ISO (review of previous actions, internal audit results, risk assessments, KPIs, continual improvement opportunities). Retain signed meeting minutes as evidence.

isoDesc: The organization shall continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the information security management system.
name: Continual improvement
notes: Evidence that the ISMS is maturing over time. Pull examples from management reviews, audit findings, and completed risk treatment plans demonstrating that the organization's security posture is stronger today than it was a year ago.

isoDesc: When a nonconformity occurs, the organization shall react to the nonconformity, evaluate the need for action to eliminate causes, and implement corrective actions.
name: Nonconformity and corrective action
notes: Maintain a 'Corrective Action Register' (CAR) or root-cause tracking system. When an internal audit, external audit, or incident reveals a failure, formally log it, perform root cause analysis (e.g., 5 Whys), assign corrective tasks, and verify they resolved the root cause.

isoDesc: Information security policy and topic-specific policies should be defined, approved by management, published, communicated to and acknowledged by relevant personnel and relevant interested parties, and reviewed at planned intervals and if significant changes occur.
name: Policies for information security
notes: Establish a top-level information security policy approved by senior management, supported by topic-specific policies (e.g. access control, data classification, incident response). Review at least annually or after significant changes. Ensure policies are communicated to all staff, contractors, and relevant third parties. Map each policy to specific framework requirements across ISO 27001, NIST CSF, SOC 2, and PCI DSS to demonstrate cross-framework alignment during audits.

isoDesc: Information security roles and responsibilities should be defined and allocated according to the organization needs.
name: Information security roles and responsibilities
notes: Define a RACI matrix covering all information security functions including risk management, incident response, compliance monitoring, and security architecture. Assign an Information Security Manager or CISO with clear authority. Ensure segregation between those who authorise, implement, and review security controls. Document reporting lines to senior management and the board. Review role assignments during organisational restructures.

isoDesc: Conflicting duties and conflicting areas of responsibility should be segregated.
name: Segregation of duties
notes: Implement segregation of duties to prevent any single individual from controlling all aspects of a critical process. Map critical business processes and identify conflict-of-interest pairs (e.g. change approval vs. deployment, user provisioning vs. access review). Where segregation is not feasible due to team size, implement compensating controls such as enhanced logging, management review, and dual authorisation for high-risk actions.

isoDesc: Management should require all personnel to apply information security in accordance with the established information security policy, topic-specific policies and procedures of the organization.
name: Management responsibilities
notes: Ensure management at all levels actively demonstrate support for information security through resource allocation, participation in security governance forums, and leading by example. Management should sign off on security policies, attend security briefings, and champion security awareness initiatives. Include information security responsibilities in job descriptions and performance reviews for managers.

isoDesc: The organization should establish and maintain contact with relevant authorities.
name: Contact with authorities
notes: Maintain a register of relevant authorities including the ICO (data protection), NCSC (cyber incidents), sector-specific regulators (FCA, OFCOM etc.), and law enforcement contacts. Define clear thresholds and procedures for when to engage each authority. Ensure incident response playbooks include authority notification timelines (e.g. ICO 72-hour breach notification). Test contact procedures during tabletop exercises.

isoDesc: The organization should establish and maintain contact with special interest groups or other specialist security forums and professional associations.
name: Contact with special interest groups
notes: Join relevant information sharing communities such as CiSP (NCSC), sector-specific ISACs, OWASP chapters, Cloud Security Alliance, and vendor security advisory lists. Assign responsibility for monitoring threat feeds and sharing actionable intelligence internally. Participate actively rather than passively — contribute anonymised threat data and attend community meetings. Use insights to update risk assessments and security controls.

isoDesc: Information relating to information security threats should be collected and analysed to produce threat intelligence.
name: Threat intelligence
notes: Establish a threat intelligence capability that ingests data from multiple sources: commercial feeds, open source (OSINT), government advisories (NCSC, CISA), industry ISACs, and dark web monitoring. Contextualise intelligence against your asset inventory and risk profile. Integrate threat intelligence into vulnerability management prioritisation, SOC alert tuning, and risk assessment processes. Review and update threat landscape assessments quarterly.

isoDesc: Information security should be integrated into project management.
name: Information security in project management
notes: Embed security checkpoints at each project phase: initiation (security requirements), design (threat modelling), build (secure coding standards), test (security testing), and deployment (hardening checklists). Require a security impact assessment for all projects handling sensitive data or modifying critical systems. Include security sign-off as a gate criterion before go-live. Track security debt from projects in a centralised register.

isoDesc: An inventory of information and other associated assets, including owners, should be developed and maintained.
name: Inventory of information and other associated assets
notes: Maintain a comprehensive asset inventory covering hardware (servers, endpoints, network devices, IoT), software (applications, SaaS, licenses), data assets (databases, file shares, cloud storage), and cloud resources (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS accounts). Automate discovery using CMDB tools, network scanning, and cloud API integration. Assign owners to every asset. Review and reconcile the inventory at least quarterly. Link assets to business processes and data classification levels.

isoDesc: Rules for the acceptable use and procedures for handling information and other associated assets should be identified, documented and implemented.
name: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
notes: Develop an Acceptable Use Policy covering use of corporate devices, email, internet, social media, personal devices (BYOD), removable media, and cloud services. Include clear rules on prohibited activities, data handling expectations, and consequences of violations. Require all staff and contractors to acknowledge the AUP during onboarding and annually thereafter. Update the AUP to address emerging technologies and work patterns (e.g. AI tools, remote working).

isoDesc: Personnel and other interested parties as appropriate should return all the organization's assets in their possession upon change or termination of their employment, contract or agreement.
name: Return of assets
notes: Include asset return in the formal offboarding checklist covering laptops, mobile devices, access cards, tokens, keys, and any company data on personal devices. Verify return within the employee's notice period. For remote workers, arrange courier collection or office drop-off. Wipe and re-image returned devices before reissue. Coordinate with IT, HR, and facilities to ensure nothing is missed. Document the process with sign-off from the leaver and their manager.

isoDesc: Information should be classified according to the information security needs of the organization based on confidentiality, integrity, availability and relevant interested party requirements.
name: Classification of information
notes: Define a data classification scheme with clear levels (e.g. Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) and criteria for each. Map classification to handling requirements: storage encryption, access controls, sharing restrictions, and retention periods. Provide training and practical examples to help staff classify data correctly. Assign data owners responsible for classification decisions. Review classifications when data is repurposed or shared with new parties.

isoDesc: An appropriate set of procedures for information labelling should be developed and implemented in accordance with the information classification scheme adopted by the organization.
name: Labelling of information
notes: Implement labelling mechanisms that match your classification scheme: email headers/footers, document watermarks, file metadata tags, and database field-level labels. Automate labelling using Microsoft Information Protection, Google DLP, or equivalent tools. Ensure labels persist when data is copied, shared, or transformed. Train staff to apply labels manually where automation is not possible. Regularly audit labelling compliance.

isoDesc: Information transfer rules, procedures, or agreements should be in place for all types of transfer facilities within the organization and between the organization and other parties.
name: Information transfer
notes: Define secure transfer procedures for each channel: encrypted email (TLS/S-MIME), secure file sharing platforms (not personal cloud accounts), SFTP for batch transfers, and encrypted APIs for system-to-system. Prohibit transfer of Confidential/Restricted data via unencrypted channels. Implement DLP rules to detect and block policy violations. Maintain transfer agreements with third parties specifying security requirements. Log and monitor all transfers of sensitive data.

isoDesc: Rules to control physical and logical access to information and other associated assets should be established and implemented based on business and information security requirements.
name: Access control
notes: Implement access control based on the principle of least privilege and need-to-know. Define an access control policy covering authentication, authorisation, and accounting requirements. Use role-based access control (RBAC) as the baseline, supplemented by attribute-based access control (ABAC) for complex scenarios. Require formal access requests with manager and data owner approval. Conduct quarterly access reviews for critical systems and annual reviews for all others.

isoDesc: The full life cycle of identities should be managed.
name: Identity management
notes: Establish a formal identity lifecycle process covering joiners (provisioning), movers (role changes), and leavers (deprovisioning). Integrate with HR systems to trigger automated workflows. Verify identity before issuing credentials using government-issued ID or equivalent. Implement unique user IDs — prohibit shared or generic accounts. Maintain a central identity directory (e.g. Azure AD, Okta) as the single source of truth. Disable accounts within 24 hours of termination.

isoDesc: Allocation and management of authentication information should be controlled by a management process, including advising personnel on the appropriate handling of authentication information.
name: Authentication information
notes: Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all remote access, privileged accounts, cloud services, and email. Implement a strong password policy: minimum 12 characters, complexity requirements, and prohibition of known breached passwords. Deploy a password manager for staff. Manage service account credentials in a secrets vault (e.g. HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) with automatic rotation. Prohibit hardcoded credentials in source code.

isoDesc: Access rights to information and other associated assets should be provisioned, reviewed, modified and removed in accordance with the organization's topic-specific policy on and rules for access control.
name: Access rights
notes: Conduct quarterly access reviews for privileged and high-risk systems, and annual reviews for all other systems. Verify that access rights match current roles and responsibilities. Remove orphaned accounts, excessive privileges, and access for leavers. Implement automated access certification campaigns using identity governance tools. Require re-approval for access rights that have not been used within 90 days. Document review outcomes and remediation actions.

isoDesc: Processes and procedures should be defined and implemented to manage the information security risks associated with the use of supplier's products or services.
name: Information security in supplier relationships
notes: Establish a supplier security assessment framework with risk-based tiers (Critical, High, Medium, Low) based on data access, system integration, and business dependency. Require security questionnaires, SOC 2 reports, ISO 27001 certificates, or penetration test results based on tier. Include information security requirements in procurement processes. Maintain a supplier risk register. Conduct due diligence before onboarding and ongoing monitoring thereafter.

isoDesc: Relevant information security requirements should be established and agreed with each supplier based on the type of supplier relationship.
name: Addressing info security within supplier agreements
notes: Include specific security clauses in all supplier contracts: data protection obligations, right to audit, breach notification timelines (e.g. 24-48 hours), subcontractor flow-down requirements, data return/destruction on termination, and compliance with applicable regulations (GDPR, PCI DSS). Define service levels for security-relevant metrics. Require evidence of security controls (e.g. annual SOC 2 reports). Include termination provisions for material security failures.

isoDesc: Processes and procedures should be defined and implemented to manage the information security risks associated with the ICT products and services supply chain.
name: Managing info security in the ICT supply chain
notes: Map your ICT supply chain to identify fourth-party dependencies and single points of failure. Require suppliers to maintain Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) for critical software. Assess risks from supply chain attacks (e.g. SolarWinds-style compromises). Implement code signing and integrity verification for software updates. Monitor supplier security posture using continuous monitoring tools (e.g. SecurityScorecard, BitSight). Include supply chain scenarios in business continuity planning.

isoDesc: The organization should regularly monitor, review, evaluate and manage change in supplier information security practices and service delivery.
name: Monitoring, review & change mgmt of supplier services
notes: Conduct at least annual reviews of critical supplier security posture. Monitor for changes in supplier risk profile: acquisitions, breaches, financial instability, or regulatory actions. Require suppliers to notify you of material security changes. Review and update security requirements when contracts are renewed. Assess the impact of supplier changes on your security controls. Maintain documentation of all review outcomes and follow-up actions.

isoDesc: Processes for acquisition, use, management and exit from cloud services should be established in accordance with the organization's information security requirements.
name: Information security for use of cloud services
notes: Implement a cloud security governance framework covering provider selection, configuration standards, data residency requirements, and shared responsibility model documentation. Require CSA STAR certification or SOC 2 reports for cloud providers. Implement cloud security posture management (CSPM) tools. Define and enforce cloud security baselines (e.g. CIS Benchmarks for AWS/Azure/GCP). Monitor for misconfigurations, exposed storage, and excessive permissions. Encrypt data at rest and in transit.

isoDesc: The organization should plan and prepare for managing information security incidents by defining, establishing and communicating information security incident management processes, roles and responsibilities.
name: Incident management planning and preparation
notes: Develop incident response playbooks for common scenarios: ransomware, data breach, DDoS, insider threat, supply chain compromise, and business email compromise. Define incident severity levels and escalation paths. Establish an incident response team with clear roles (Incident Commander, Technical Lead, Communications Lead, Legal). Maintain an out-of-hours contact list. Ensure playbooks include regulatory notification requirements. Test plans through tabletop exercises at least twice yearly.

isoDesc: The organization should assess information security events and decide if they are to be categorized as information security incidents.
name: Assessment and decision on security events
nistSub: DE.AE-02, DE.AE-03, DE.AE-04, DE.AE-06, DE.AE-08, RS.AN-08
notes: Define clear criteria for triaging security events into categories: false positive, informational, investigation required, or confirmed incident. Implement automated correlation and enrichment in your SIEM to reduce analyst workload. Establish escalation thresholds based on asset criticality, data sensitivity, and attack type. Document triage decisions and rationale. Maintain a security event taxonomy aligned with MITRE ATT&CK for consistent categorisation.

isoDesc: Information security incidents should be responded to in accordance with the documented procedures.
name: Response to information security incidents
notes: Follow a structured response methodology: Preparation, Identification, Containment (short-term and long-term), Eradication, Recovery, and Lessons Learned. Define containment strategies for different incident types (e.g. network isolation for ransomware, credential reset for account compromise). Coordinate response across IT, security, legal, communications, and HR. Preserve forensic evidence before remediation. Communicate with affected stakeholders in accordance with your communications plan.

isoDesc: Knowledge gained from information security incidents should be used to strengthen and improve the information security controls.
name: Learning from information security incidents
notes: Conduct a formal post-incident review (PIR) within two weeks of incident closure. Use a blameless approach focusing on systemic improvements rather than individual fault. Document root cause analysis, timeline of events, what worked well, what needs improvement, and specific action items with owners and deadlines. Track remediation to completion. Share anonymised lessons across the organisation. Update playbooks, detection rules, and controls based on findings.

isoDesc: The organization should establish and implement procedures for the identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of evidence related to information security events.
name: Collection of evidence
notes: Establish forensic readiness procedures including evidence preservation protocols, chain of custody documentation, and approved forensic tools. Train incident responders in evidence handling. Enable sufficient logging and retention to support investigations. Engage specialist forensic providers on retainer for complex incidents. Ensure evidence collection methods are legally admissible. Document all forensic activities with timestamps and investigator details.

isoDesc: The organization should plan how to maintain information security at an appropriate level during disruption.
name: Information security during disruption
notes: Integrate information security requirements into business continuity plans (BCP) and disaster recovery (DR) plans. Ensure security controls remain effective during disruption — avoid reducing security posture for operational convenience. Address scenarios where primary security infrastructure is unavailable. Include cybersecurity incidents (e.g. ransomware) in BCP scenarios. Test failover security controls during DR exercises. Document alternative security procedures for degraded operations.

isoDesc: ICT readiness should be planned, implemented, maintained and tested based on business continuity objectives and ICT continuity requirements.
name: ICT readiness for business continuity
notes: Define Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) for all critical systems based on business impact analysis. Implement DR solutions that meet these targets: hot standby for critical systems, warm standby for important systems, and cold backups for others. Test recovery procedures at least annually with realistic scenarios. Document recovery runbooks with step-by-step instructions. Verify data integrity after restoration. Maintain off-site and offline backup copies to protect against ransomware.

isoDesc: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements relevant to information security and the organization's approach to meet these requirements should be identified, documented and kept up to date.
name: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
notes: Maintain a register of all applicable legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements covering data protection (GDPR, DPA 2018), sector regulations (FCA, NHS DSPT), cyber regulations (NIS2), payment standards (PCI DSS), and contractual obligations. Assign owners for each requirement. Monitor for regulatory changes and assess impact. Map requirements to specific security controls to demonstrate compliance. Review the register at least annually and after significant regulatory changes.

isoDesc: The organization should implement appropriate procedures to protect intellectual property rights.
name: Intellectual property rights
notes: Maintain a software licence register covering all commercial, open-source, and SaaS licences. Implement software asset management (SAM) tools to track licence usage and compliance. Include IP clauses in employment contracts covering ownership of work product. Define procedures for using open-source software including licence compatibility checks. Train developers on IP obligations. Conduct periodic licence compliance audits.

isoDesc: Records should be protected from loss, destruction, falsification, unauthorized access and unauthorized release.
name: Protection of records
notes: Define retention schedules for all record types based on legal requirements, regulatory obligations, and business needs. Implement automated retention and deletion policies in document management systems, email, and databases. Protect records from unauthorised modification or deletion using write-once storage, access controls, and integrity checking. Ensure records are recoverable within required timeframes. Document secure destruction procedures including certificates of destruction for physical media.

isoDesc: The organization should identify and meet the requirements regarding the preservation of privacy and protection of PII according to applicable laws and regulations and contractual requirements.
name: Privacy and protection of PII
notes: Conduct Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) for high-risk processing activities. Implement privacy by design and by default in all systems processing personal data. Maintain Records of Processing Activities (ROPA). Implement data subject rights procedures (access, erasure, portability, objection). Deploy data discovery and classification tools to locate PII across systems. Minimise data collection and retention. Encrypt PII at rest and in transit. Appoint a Data Protection Officer where required.

isoDesc: The organization's approach to managing information security and its implementation including people, processes and technologies should be reviewed independently at planned intervals, or when significant changes occur.
name: Independent review of information security
notes: Commission independent reviews of the ISMS at planned intervals: internal audits at least annually covering all domains, external certification audits per the ISO 27001 cycle, and penetration testing at least annually or after significant changes. Ensure auditors are independent from the areas being reviewed. Track audit findings to closure with evidence of remediation. Report audit results to senior management and the board. Use audit findings to drive continuous improvement.

isoDesc: Compliance with the organization's information security policy, topic-specific policies, rules and standards should be regularly reviewed.
name: Compliance with policies, rules and standards
notes: Implement a compliance monitoring programme with regular self-assessments against all applicable frameworks and standards. Use automated compliance scanning tools for technical controls (e.g. CIS benchmarks, cloud configuration). Maintain a compliance dashboard showing status across all frameworks. Conduct gap assessments when new requirements emerge. Track non-conformities with root cause analysis and corrective action plans. Report compliance status to senior management quarterly.

isoDesc: Operating procedures for information processing facilities should be documented and made available to personnel who need them.
name: Documented operating procedures
notes: Develop Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for all security-critical processes: user provisioning/deprovisioning, backup and restore, patch management, incident response, change management, vulnerability scanning, and log review. Include step-by-step instructions, responsible roles, escalation procedures, and expected outcomes. Version control all procedures and review at least annually. Ensure SOPs are accessible to all relevant staff. Test procedures through regular drills.

isoDesc: Background verification checks on all candidates to become personnel should be carried out prior to joining the organization and on an ongoing basis taking into consideration applicable laws, regulations and ethics and proportional to the business requirements, the classification of the information to be accessed and the perceived risks.
name: Screening
notes: Screen all candidates before employment using identity verification, criminal records checks (DBS), reference checks, qualification verification, and credit checks where appropriate for the role. Apply enhanced screening (e.g. BS 7858) for roles with access to sensitive data or critical systems. Re-screen personnel when they move to higher-trust roles. Extend screening requirements to contractors and temporary staff through contractual agreements with agencies.

isoDesc: The employment contractual agreements should state the personnel's and the organization's responsibilities for information security.
name: Terms and conditions of employment
notes: Include information security responsibilities in employment contracts and job descriptions. Require staff to sign acceptable use policies, non-disclosure agreements, and data protection acknowledgements. Clearly state consequences of security policy violations. Cover obligations that continue after employment ends (e.g. confidentiality, return of assets, data handling). Review terms when roles change significantly. Ensure contractor agreements include equivalent security obligations.

isoDesc: Personnel of the organization and relevant interested parties should receive appropriate information security awareness, education and training and regular updates of the organization's information security policy, topic-specific policies and procedures, as relevant for their job function.
name: Information security awareness, education and training
notes: Deliver a multi-layered security awareness programme: mandatory induction training for new starters, annual refresher training for all staff, role-based training for privileged users and developers, and continuous reinforcement through simulated phishing campaigns, newsletters, and security champions. Measure effectiveness through completion rates, phishing simulation results, and security incident trends. Tailor content to current threats and recent incidents. Require completion as a condition of continued system access.

isoDesc: A disciplinary process should be formalized and communicated to take action against personnel and other relevant interested parties who have committed an information security policy violation.
name: Disciplinary process
notes: Define a clear, documented disciplinary process for security policy violations, graduated from informal warnings to formal action depending on severity and intent. Ensure the process is fair, consistent, and aligned with employment law. Involve HR and legal in serious cases. Communicate the existence of the process to all staff as a deterrent. Document all disciplinary actions and outcomes. Use incidents as learning opportunities where appropriate.

isoDesc: Information security responsibilities and duties that remain valid after termination or change of employment should be defined, enforced and communicated to relevant personnel and other interested parties.
name: Responsibilities after termination or change
notes: Define post-employment/engagement obligations in contracts including ongoing confidentiality, non-compete clauses where applicable, return of all information and assets, and secure deletion of company data from personal devices. Conduct exit interviews covering security obligations. Ensure all access is revoked on or before the last day. Monitor for data exfiltration during the notice period for high-risk departures. Maintain records of offboarding completion.

isoDesc: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements reflecting the organization's needs for the protection of information should be identified, documented, regularly reviewed and signed by personnel and other relevant interested parties.
name: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
notes: Require NDAs or confidentiality clauses for all staff, contractors, consultants, and third parties with access to confidential information. Tailor NDA scope to the specific information and duration of engagement. Review and refresh NDAs when roles change or when access to new categories of information is granted. Ensure NDAs are legally enforceable in relevant jurisdictions. Maintain a register of signed NDAs with expiry dates.

isoDesc: Security measures should be implemented when personnel are working remotely to protect information accessed, processed or stored outside the organization's premises.
name: Remote working
notes: Establish a remote working security policy covering: mandatory VPN for corporate network access, endpoint protection requirements (EDR, disk encryption, up-to-date patching), secure Wi-Fi requirements (WPA3, no public Wi-Fi for sensitive work), physical security of devices and documents, approved collaboration tools, and clear desk/clear screen at home. Provide equipment that meets security standards. Conduct periodic remote security assessments. Address the risks of co-working spaces and public transport.

isoDesc: The organization should provide a mechanism for personnel to report observed or suspected information security events through appropriate channels in a timely manner.
name: Information security event reporting
notes: Establish clear, accessible channels for reporting security events: dedicated email address, internal ticketing system, phone hotline, and anonymous reporting option. Ensure all staff know how to recognise and report potential security events. Set expectations for response times. Protect reporters from retaliation. Acknowledge reports promptly and provide feedback on outcomes. Track reporting metrics as an indicator of security culture maturity.

isoDesc: Security perimeters should be defined and used to protect areas that contain information and other associated assets.
name: Physical security perimeters
notes: Define physical security zones based on sensitivity: public areas, staff-only areas, restricted areas (server rooms, data centres), and high-security areas (safes, secure rooms). Implement appropriate controls at each perimeter: reception desks, access card readers, biometric scanners, mantraps, and anti-tailgating measures. Monitor perimeter access points with CCTV. Conduct regular physical security assessments. Ensure perimeter controls are resilient to common bypass techniques.

isoDesc: Secure areas should be protected by appropriate entry controls and access points.
name: Physical entry
notes: Implement multi-factor physical access control for restricted areas: access card plus PIN or biometric. Maintain visitor management procedures: pre-registration, ID verification, badge issuance, escort requirements, and sign-out. Log all physical access with timestamps and retain logs for at least 90 days. Conduct regular reviews of physical access rights. Immediately revoke access for terminated personnel. Test access controls regularly to identify tailgating or bypass risks.

isoDesc: Physical security for offices, rooms and facilities should be designed and implemented.
name: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
notes: Secure server rooms, network closets, and sensitive areas with reinforced walls, security-rated doors, and monitored locks. Ensure offices containing sensitive equipment or documents are locked when unoccupied. Implement clean desk policy enforcement. Restrict knowledge of sensitive area locations to need-to-know personnel. Install intruder alarms with 24/7 monitoring. Conduct regular physical security walkthroughs.

isoDesc: Premises should be continuously monitored for unauthorized physical access.
name: Physical security monitoring
notes: Deploy CCTV coverage at all entry/exit points, perimeters, server rooms, and other sensitive areas. Ensure cameras provide sufficient resolution for identification. Implement 24/7 monitoring or AI-based alerting for out-of-hours activity. Retain CCTV footage for a minimum of 30 days. Protect camera systems from tampering and unauthorised access. Complement CCTV with intruder detection systems and security patrols. Ensure compliance with GDPR and surveillance camera codes of practice.

isoDesc: Protection against physical and environmental threats, such as natural disasters and other intentional or unintentional physical threats to infrastructure should be designed and implemented.
name: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
notes: Implement environmental controls appropriate to the risk: fire detection and suppression (FM-200, inert gas for server rooms), flood detection and drainage, temperature and humidity monitoring, earthquake protection where applicable, and protection against electromagnetic interference. Maintain environmental monitoring with automated alerting. Test fire suppression and detection systems at least annually. Ensure insurance coverage reflects environmental risks.

isoDesc: Security measures for working in secure areas should be designed and implemented.
name: Working in secure areas
notes: Restrict activities in secure areas: no photography, no personal mobile devices, supervised access for visitors and contractors, requirement to display ID at all times, and prohibition of unaccompanied work outside business hours. Maintain access logs for secure areas. Limit knowledge of secure area locations and contents. Conduct regular sweeps for unauthorised devices. Brief all personnel on secure area rules before granting access.

isoDesc: Clear desk rules for papers and removable storage media and clear screen rules for information processing facilities should be defined and appropriately enforced.
name: Clear desk and clear screen
notes: Enforce clear desk and clear screen as mandatory policy: lock screens after 5 minutes of inactivity (enforced via GPO/MDM), secure sensitive documents in locked drawers/cabinets when not in use, use privacy screens on devices in shared or public areas, shred rather than bin paper documents, and clear whiteboards after meetings. Conduct regular compliance checks with spot audits. Include clear desk/screen in security awareness training.

isoDesc: Equipment should be sited securely and protected.
name: Equipment siting and protection
notes: Position critical equipment (servers, networking, UPS) in secure, access-controlled rooms with appropriate environmental controls. Protect cable runs from damage and unauthorised access. Ensure adequate cooling, power, and ventilation. Position monitors away from windows to prevent visual eavesdropping. Secure portable equipment with cable locks when unattended. Implement environmental monitoring with automated alerts for temperature, humidity, and water ingress.

isoDesc: Information and other associated assets off-premises should be protected.
name: Security of assets off-premises
notes: Define security requirements for equipment used outside company premises: mandatory full-disk encryption, VPN for all corporate access, remote wipe capability, physical security awareness (never leave unattended in vehicles or public places). Prohibit storage of Confidential/Restricted data on removable media without encryption. Require incident reporting within 4 hours of loss or theft. Include off-premises security in staff awareness training.

isoDesc: Storage media should be managed through their life cycle of acquisition, use, transportation and disposal in accordance with the organization's classification scheme and handling requirements.
name: Storage media
notes: Classify storage media (USB drives, external HDDs, tapes, optical media) according to the sensitivity of data stored. Encrypt all media containing Confidential or Restricted data using AES-256 or equivalent. Maintain a register of removable media with assigned owners. Implement port control to restrict unauthorised USB device usage. Define secure transportation procedures for media in transit. Conduct certified destruction (NIST 800-88) for media at end of life with certificates of destruction.

isoDesc: Information processing facilities should be protected from power failures and other disruptions caused by failures in supporting utilities.
name: Supporting utilities
notes: Provide redundant power supplies for critical infrastructure: dual utility feeds where possible, UPS systems sized for at least 15-30 minutes runtime, diesel generators with automatic failover and fuel for 48+ hours. Monitor UPS battery health and replace on schedule. Implement redundant cooling systems. Test failover to backup power quarterly. Ensure supporting utilities (water, telecoms) have appropriate resilience. Document all utility dependencies and single points of failure.

isoDesc: Cables carrying power, data or supporting information services should be protected from interception, interference or damage.
name: Cabling security
notes: Route data cabling through secure conduits, avoiding public areas where possible. Use fibre optic cables for sensitive links to prevent electromagnetic eavesdropping. Separate power and data cabling to prevent interference. Label and document all cabling. Secure patch panels and distribution frames in locked cabinets. Implement network access control (802.1X) to prevent unauthorised device connection. Regularly audit cable infrastructure for unauthorised connections.

isoDesc: Equipment should be maintained correctly to ensure availability, integrity and confidentiality of information.
name: Equipment maintenance
notes: Establish a preventive maintenance schedule for all critical equipment aligned with manufacturer recommendations. Restrict maintenance to authorised personnel — verify identity and authorisation before granting access. Supervise third-party maintenance engineers in sensitive areas. Maintain maintenance logs with details of work performed. Verify equipment integrity after maintenance. Address security implications of maintenance — ensure sensitive data is protected when equipment is serviced off-site.

isoDesc: Items of equipment containing storage media should be verified to ensure that any sensitive data and licensed software has been removed or securely overwritten prior to disposal or re-use.
name: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
notes: Follow NIST SP 800-88 guidelines for media sanitisation: Clear (logical overwrite), Purge (cryptographic erase or degauss), or Destroy (shred, incinerate, disintegrate) based on data sensitivity. Verify sanitisation before releasing equipment for reuse or disposal. Obtain certificates of destruction from contracted disposal providers. Maintain an auditable trail from asset register to destruction certificate. Consider environmental regulations for electronic waste disposal.

isoDesc: Information stored on, processed by or routed via user endpoint devices should be protected.
name: User endpoint devices
notes: Deploy a comprehensive endpoint protection stack: endpoint detection and response (EDR/XDR), full-disk encryption (BitLocker/FileVault), mobile device management (MDM) for configuration enforcement, automated patching, application whitelisting for high-security environments, and host-based firewall. Enforce security baselines using CIS Benchmarks. Implement network access control to quarantine non-compliant devices. Monitor endpoint health continuously and remediate non-compliance within defined SLAs.

isoDesc: The allocation and use of privileged access rights should be restricted and managed.
name: Privileged access rights
notes: Implement a Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution covering: vaulting of privileged credentials, session recording and monitoring, just-in-time access provisioning, automatic credential rotation, and break-glass procedures for emergencies. Enforce MFA for all privileged access. Separate privileged and standard user accounts. Conduct quarterly reviews of privileged access. Monitor for anomalous privileged account behaviour. Minimise the number of standing privileged accounts.

isoDesc: Access to information and other associated assets should be restricted in accordance with the established topic-specific policy on access control.
name: Information access restriction
notes: Implement role-based access control (RBAC) as the foundation, supplemented by attribute-based access control (ABAC) for context-sensitive decisions (location, device, time). Enforce access restrictions at application, database, and file system levels. Implement row-level and column-level security for sensitive database fields. Use API gateways to enforce access policies for service-to-service communication. Log all access to sensitive data. Deny by default — require explicit authorisation for all access.

isoDesc: Read and write access to source code, development tools and software libraries should be appropriately managed.
name: Access to source code
notes: Store all source code in managed repositories (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket) with access restricted to authorised developers. Enforce branch protection rules: require pull request reviews, prevent force pushes to main/production branches, and require CI/CD pipeline passes before merge. Implement code signing for production deployments. Scan repositories for secrets and credentials using automated tools. Restrict access to production deployment pipelines. Audit repository access quarterly.

isoDesc: Secure authentication technologies and procedures should be implemented based on information access restrictions and the topic-specific policy on access control.
name: Secure authentication
notes: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all users, prioritising phishing-resistant methods (FIDO2/WebAuthn, hardware security keys) for privileged users and externally-facing systems. Deploy SSO to centralise authentication and reduce password fatigue. Implement adaptive/risk-based authentication that increases assurance for unusual access patterns. Support passwordless authentication where possible. Monitor for credential stuffing and brute force attacks. Enforce account lockout after failed attempts.

isoDesc: The use of resources should be monitored and adjusted in line with current and projected capacity requirements.
name: Capacity management
notes: Monitor capacity utilisation across compute, storage, network, and licensing dimensions. Implement auto-scaling for cloud workloads with defined upper limits to prevent cost runaway. Set alerting thresholds at 70% and 85% utilisation. Conduct capacity planning reviews quarterly, incorporating growth projections and planned changes. Address capacity-related availability risks in business continuity planning. Monitor for anomalous resource consumption that could indicate cryptomining or DDoS.

isoDesc: Protection against malware should be implemented and supported by appropriate user awareness.
name: Protection against malware
notes: Deploy a defence-in-depth malware protection strategy: EDR/XDR on all endpoints, email gateway filtering with attachment sandboxing, web proxy with malware scanning, network-level detection (IDS/IPS), and application whitelisting for high-security systems. Ensure signatures and engines update automatically. Configure real-time scanning plus scheduled full scans. Block execution of scripts and macros by default — whitelist by exception. Monitor for fileless malware and living-off-the-land techniques.

isoDesc: Information about technical vulnerabilities of information systems in use should be obtained, the organization's exposure to such vulnerabilities should be evaluated and appropriate measures should be taken.
name: Management of technical vulnerabilities
notes: Implement a comprehensive vulnerability management programme: automated scanning at least weekly for external-facing assets and monthly for internal assets, prioritisation using CVSS plus asset criticality and exploit availability, defined remediation SLAs (Critical: 48 hours, High: 7 days, Medium: 30 days, Low: 90 days), and exception management with risk acceptance sign-off. Subscribe to vendor security advisories. Conduct annual penetration testing. Track vulnerability trends and patch compliance metrics.

isoDesc: Configurations, including security configurations, of hardware, software, services and networks should be established, documented, implemented, monitored and reviewed.
name: Configuration management
notes: Establish security configuration baselines for all technology platforms using CIS Benchmarks or vendor hardening guides. Automate configuration deployment using infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Ansible, GPO). Implement continuous configuration monitoring using CSPM (cloud) and compliance scanning tools. Detect and remediate configuration drift automatically. Disable unnecessary services, ports, and default accounts. Document and approve any deviations from baselines. Review baselines annually.

isoDesc: Information stored in information systems, devices or in any other storage media should be deleted when no longer required.
name: Information deletion
notes: Implement automated data retention and deletion policies based on the retention schedule. Ensure deletion is irreversible — use cryptographic erasure for encrypted data, secure overwrite for unencrypted data. Extend deletion to all copies including backups, replicas, archives, and cloud storage. Address data in SaaS applications and third-party systems. Implement user-initiated deletion for data subject erasure requests (GDPR Article 17). Maintain deletion logs as evidence of compliance.

isoDesc: Data masking should be used in accordance with the organization's topic-specific policy on access control and other related topic-specific policies, and business requirements, taking into consideration applicable legislation.
name: Data masking
notes: Implement data masking and pseudonymisation for non-production environments (development, testing, training, analytics). Use irreversible masking techniques for non-production data. Deploy dynamic data masking for production databases to restrict what users can see based on their role. Implement tokenisation for payment card data (PCI DSS compliance). Ensure masked data maintains referential integrity and statistical properties for valid testing. Document masking rules and regularly verify effectiveness.

isoDesc: Data leakage prevention measures should be applied to systems, networks and any other devices that process, store or transmit sensitive information.
name: Data leakage prevention
notes: Deploy DLP controls across all data channels: endpoint DLP for USB/print/clipboard, email DLP for outbound sensitive data, cloud DLP for SaaS and cloud storage, and network DLP for web uploads. Define DLP policies based on data classification: monitor for Internal data, block for Confidential/Restricted data. Integrate with data classification labels. Tune policies to minimise false positives. Establish a DLP incident review process. Report DLP metrics to management monthly.

isoDesc: Backup copies of information, software and systems should be maintained and regularly tested in accordance with the agreed topic-specific policy on backup.
name: Information backup
notes: Implement the 3-2-1-1-0 backup strategy: 3 copies of data, on 2 different media types, with 1 off-site copy, 1 offline/immutable copy (ransomware protection), and 0 errors after verification. Automate backup verification with integrity checks and test restores. Define backup schedules aligned with RPO requirements. Encrypt backups at rest and in transit. Test full system restoration at least annually. Document restore procedures with step-by-step runbooks. Monitor backup success/failure rates daily.

isoDesc: Information processing facilities should be implemented with redundancy sufficient to meet availability requirements.
name: Redundancy of information processing facilities
notes: Implement redundancy at all critical layers: active-active or active-passive clusters for applications, database replication (synchronous for zero data loss, asynchronous for geo-redundancy), redundant network paths with automatic failover, and multi-region deployment for cloud workloads. Eliminate single points of failure for critical services. Test failover procedures at least annually. Monitor replication lag and failover health continuously. Document recovery procedures for each redundancy mechanism.

isoDesc: Logs that record activities, exceptions, faults and other relevant events should be produced, stored, protected and analysed.
name: Logging
notes: Centralise log collection in a SIEM platform ingesting logs from all critical sources: authentication systems, firewalls, IDS/IPS, EDR, cloud platforms, applications, databases, and physical access systems. Define log retention periods: minimum 12 months online, longer in archive for compliance (PCI DSS requires 12 months). Protect log integrity using write-once storage or cryptographic hashing. Ensure logs include who, what, when, where, and outcome. Synchronise time sources across all systems.

isoDesc: Networks, systems and applications should be monitored for anomalous behaviour and appropriate actions taken to evaluate potential information security incidents.
name: Monitoring activities
notes: Establish 24/7 security monitoring capability through an internal SOC or managed service (MSSP/MDR). Define detection use cases aligned with MITRE ATT&CK framework covering initial access, execution, persistence, privilege escalation, lateral movement, and data exfiltration. Implement automated alerting with defined response SLAs. Tune detection rules to reduce false positives. Conduct regular purple team exercises to validate detection coverage. Monitor for both external threats and insider risk indicators.

isoDesc: The clocks of information processing systems used by the organization should be synchronized to approved time sources.
name: Clock synchronisation
notes: Configure all systems to synchronise time from authoritative NTP sources (e.g. NIST, NPL, GPS). Implement a tiered NTP architecture with redundant stratum-1 sources. Monitor for time drift and alert when synchronisation fails. Ensure all log timestamps use a consistent timezone format (UTC recommended). Time synchronisation is critical for log correlation, forensic investigations, and compliance with audit requirements. Document the NTP architecture and monitor source integrity.

isoDesc: The use of utility programs that can be capable of overriding system and application controls should be restricted and tightly controlled.
name: Use of privileged utility programs
notes: Restrict access to privileged utility programs (system tools, diagnostic utilities, registry editors, packet sniffers) to authorised administrators only. Implement application whitelisting to prevent execution of unauthorised tools. Log all usage of privileged utilities. Remove unnecessary utilities from production systems. Require management approval for installation of new administrative tools. Monitor for use of living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins) that could indicate malicious activity.

isoDesc: Procedures and measures should be implemented to securely manage software installation on operational systems.
name: Installation of software on operational systems
notes: Implement a formal software installation policy: only authorised software from approved sources may be installed on operational systems. Maintain an approved software catalogue. Use application whitelisting or software restriction policies on production systems. Enforce code signing requirements for deployed software. Route all production deployments through CI/CD pipelines with security gates. Prohibit installation of software directly by end users on managed devices. Audit installed software regularly.

isoDesc: Networks and network devices should be secured, managed and controlled to protect information in systems and applications.
name: Networks security
notes: Implement network segmentation separating trust zones: internet-facing DMZ, internal user network, server/application tier, database tier, management network, and OT/IoT networks. Deploy next-generation firewalls with application-level inspection at zone boundaries. Implement IDS/IPS for threat detection. Monitor east-west traffic between segments, not just north-south. Conduct regular network architecture reviews. Document all firewall rules with business justification. Remove stale rules quarterly.

isoDesc: Security mechanisms, service levels and management requirements of network services should be identified, implemented and monitored.
name: Security of network services
notes: Define security requirements for all network services including SLAs for availability, incident response, and patching. Conduct security assessments of managed network service providers. Implement encrypted transport (TLS 1.2+, IPsec) for all network services. Monitor service provider compliance with security requirements. Include security provisions in network service contracts. Regularly review network service architecture for security weaknesses.

isoDesc: Groups of information services, users and information systems should be segregated in the organization's networks.
name: Segregation of networks
notes: Implement microsegmentation to limit lateral movement: VLANs for broad segmentation, software-defined networking for granular control, and zero trust network access (ZTNA) for user-to-application connectivity. Isolate high-value assets (payment systems, databases with PII) in dedicated segments. Restrict inter-segment traffic to explicitly permitted flows. Monitor for unauthorised lateral movement using network detection and response (NDR) tools. Test segmentation effectiveness through penetration testing.

isoDesc: Access to external websites should be managed to reduce exposure to malicious content.
name: Web filtering
notes: Deploy web filtering to block access to known malicious sites, command-and-control infrastructure, and policy-violating content categories. Implement DNS filtering as an additional layer (e.g. Cisco Umbrella, Cloudflare Gateway). Enforce HTTPS inspection for visibility into encrypted traffic (with appropriate privacy safeguards). Block downloads of high-risk file types. Maintain URL categorisation exceptions with business justification. Monitor web filtering logs for indicators of compromise.

isoDesc: Rules for the effective and acceptable use of cryptography, including cryptographic key management, should be defined and implemented.
name: Use of cryptography
notes: Define a cryptographic policy specifying approved algorithms (AES-256 for symmetric, RSA-2048+ or ECC for asymmetric, SHA-256+ for hashing), key management procedures, and certificate lifecycle management. Encrypt all data at rest (full-disk, database, file-level as appropriate) and in transit (TLS 1.2+ minimum). Implement a hardware security module (HSM) or cloud KMS for key protection. Automate certificate management to prevent expiry. Plan for post-quantum cryptography migration.

isoDesc: Rules for the secure development of software and systems should be established and applied.
name: Secure development life cycle
notes: Integrate security into every phase of the SDLC: threat modelling in design, secure coding standards in development (OWASP guidelines), static analysis (SAST) in build, dynamic testing (DAST) in staging, and penetration testing before production release. Implement security champions within development teams. Track security debt alongside technical debt. Require security review sign-off for all production releases. Provide regular secure development training for all developers.

isoDesc: Information security requirements should be identified, specified and approved when developing or acquiring applications.
name: Application security requirements
notes: Define application security requirements based on data sensitivity and exposure: input validation, output encoding, authentication and session management, access control, error handling, cryptographic controls, and API security. Incorporate OWASP Top 10 and ASVS (Application Security Verification Standard) as baseline requirements. Conduct threat modelling for all new applications and major changes. Require security acceptance criteria in user stories. Test security requirements as part of QA.

isoDesc: Principles for engineering secure systems should be established, documented, maintained and applied to any information system development activities.
name: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
notes: Apply defence-in-depth and zero trust principles in system architecture: never trust, always verify; assume breach; least privilege access; microsegmentation; and end-to-end encryption. Document security architecture patterns and reference architectures. Review all new system designs against security architecture principles. Implement security architecture review as a gate in the project lifecycle. Maintain an enterprise security architecture diagram. Regularly assess architecture against emerging threats.

isoDesc: Secure coding principles should be applied to software development.
name: Secure coding
notes: Enforce secure coding standards based on OWASP guidelines: input validation and output encoding to prevent injection attacks, parameterised queries for database access, secure session management, proper error handling (no sensitive data in error messages), secure file upload handling, and protection against CSRF/SSRF. Implement automated SAST tools in CI/CD pipelines. Conduct peer code reviews with security focus. Provide developers with secure coding training annually.

isoDesc: Security testing processes should be defined and implemented in the development life cycle.
name: Security testing in development and acceptance
notes: Implement a multi-layered security testing approach: SAST in CI/CD pipelines (every build), DAST in staging environments (every release), interactive application security testing (IAST) in QA, dependency scanning for vulnerable libraries (continuous), penetration testing for major releases and annually, and bug bounty programmes for externally-facing applications. Define security testing pass/fail criteria. Track and remediate findings before production deployment. Verify fixes through re-testing.

isoDesc: The organization should direct, monitor and review the activities related to outsourced system development.
name: Outsourced development
notes: Include comprehensive security requirements in outsourced development contracts: adherence to secure coding standards, security testing requirements, code review processes, intellectual property ownership, source code escrow, vulnerability management obligations, and right to conduct security assessments. Require developers to undergo security training. Review third-party code before integration. Implement software composition analysis to identify vulnerable dependencies in third-party code.

isoDesc: Development, testing and production environments should be separated and secured.
name: Separation of dev, test and production environments
notes: Maintain strictly separated environments for development, testing/staging, and production. Prohibit use of production data in non-production environments — use masked or synthetic data instead. Implement separate credentials and access controls for each environment. Restrict production access to authorised operations staff only. Use infrastructure-as-code to ensure environment parity while maintaining isolation. Monitor for configuration drift between environments. Audit cross-environment access regularly.

isoDesc: Changes to information processing facilities and information systems should be subject to change management procedures.
name: Change management
notes: Implement a formal change management process: RFC submission with business justification and security impact assessment, risk categorisation (standard, normal, emergency), CAB review for normal and significant changes, testing and rollback plan documentation, deployment window scheduling, post-implementation verification, and documentation update. Track all changes in a change management system. Audit emergency changes retrospectively. Monitor for unauthorised changes through configuration monitoring.

isoDesc: Test information should be appropriately selected, protected and managed.
name: Test information
notes: Prohibit the use of production data in test environments. Generate realistic test data using data masking, synthetic data generation, or pseudonymisation tools. Ensure test data maintains referential integrity and edge cases for valid testing. Apply the same classification and protection controls to test data as to the source data if masking is not applied. Securely destroy test data after use. Document test data handling procedures. Audit compliance with test data policies.

isoDesc: Audit tests and other assurance activities involving assessment of operational systems should be planned and agreed between the tester and appropriate management.
name: Protection of info systems during audit testing
notes: Plan audit testing activities to minimise disruption to production systems and business operations. Schedule intensive testing (e.g. penetration tests, performance tests) during maintenance windows or low-activity periods. Restrict auditor access to the minimum required — use read-only access where possible. Monitor auditor activities during testing. Ensure audit tools are approved and do not introduce vulnerabilities. Obtain sign-off from system owners before audit testing. Back up systems before destructive testing.
